```{r setup, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
# the code of the benchmark is in three scripts in the directory code (one to
# prepare the data, one to run ADMIXTURE and fastmixture, and one to run
# gt_radmix()), from which the chunks below are read (purl = FALSE
# because pkgdown purls this file from the package root when looking for
# images, where these relative paths do not exist)
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_data.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_cli.sh")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_radmix.R")
# the directory with the results of the benchmark (data/admixture_benchmark,
# or data/admixture_benchmark_quick for the results of a quick run)
results_dir <- params$results_dir
```

`gt_radmix()` estimates ancestry proportions with the method of ADMIXTURE
(Alexander et al. 2009), using a modified version of the algorithm of
OpenADMIXTURE (Ko et al. 2023), whose C++ code is largely ported from
OpenADMIXTURE.jl, directly from the backing file of a `gen_tibble`.
This article compares it with two programs that fit the same model:
ADMIXTURE itself, and fastmixture (Santander et al. 2024). Both are run from
the command line. The comparison uses the Human Genome Diversity Project
(HGDP). It checks that the three programs find the same ancestry
proportions, and measures how long each takes on 1 to 8 cores, with and
without cross-validation.

The [results](#results) come first. The second part,
[How the benchmark was run](#how-the-benchmark-was-run), describes the data
and the runs, with their code, and how to run the benchmark again.

# Results

```{r results_packages, include = FALSE}
# to summarise and plot the results
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r read_results, include = FALSE}
# the name of each program, in the order of the tables and plots
tool_labels <- c(
  radmix = "gt_radmix()",
  admixture = "ADMIXTURE",
  fastmixture = "fastmixture"
)
# one row per run, with its time, log-likelihood, cross-validation error
# and number of iterations, and the name of the files of its Q matrix and
# log (e.g. admixture_t4_cv for ADMIXTURE on 4 cores with cross-validation)
timings <- bind_rows(
  read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "timings_cli.csv")),
  read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "timings_radmix.csv"))
) %>%
  mutate(
    run = paste0(tool, "_t", n_cores, if_else(crossval, "_cv", "_nocv")),
    tool = factor(tool, names(tool_labels))
  )
# the machine and software, and the size of the data
session_cli <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "session_cli.csv"))
session_r <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "session_r.csv"))
session_value <- function(session, item) session$value[session$item == item]
n_indiv <- as.integer(session_value(session_cli, "individuals"))
n_loci <- as.integer(session_value(session_cli, "loci"))
# the population and region of the individual of each row of the Q matrices
individuals <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "individuals.csv"))
```

```{r align_q, include = FALSE}
# the Q matrix of a run
read_q <- function(run) {
  as.matrix(read.table(file.path(results_dir, "Q", paste0(run, ".Q"))))
}
# all the permutations of 1:n, one per row
permutations <- function(n) {
  if (n == 1) {
    return(matrix(1L))
  }
  smaller <- permutations(n - 1)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(first) {
    others <- setdiff(seq_len(n), first)
    cbind(first, matrix(others[smaller], ncol = n - 1))
  }))
}
# the clusters of different runs are numbered arbitrarily, so the columns of
# a Q matrix are reordered to best match those of a reference (with the
# smallest sum of squared differences, trying all the permutations)
align_q <- function(q, reference) {
  perms <- permutations(ncol(q))
  ssd <- apply(perms, 1, function(perm) sum((q[, perm] - reference)^2))
  unname(q[, perms[which.min(ssd), ]])
}
```

```{r agreement, include = FALSE}
# the reference: ADMIXTURE on the fewest cores, without cross-validation
min_cores <- min(timings$n_cores)
max_cores <- max(timings$n_cores)
reference_run <- paste0("admixture_t", min_cores, "_nocv")
q_ref <- read_q(reference_run)
k <- ncol(q_ref)
# the Q matrix of each run, with its clusters in the order of the reference
q_aligned <- lapply(
  setNames(timings$run, timings$run),
  function(run) align_q(read_q(run), q_ref)
)
max_diff <- function(a, b) max(abs(a - b))
rmse <- function(a, b) sqrt(mean((a - b)^2))
# for each run, the difference in log-likelihood from the reference, the
# largest difference in the ancestry proportions from the run of the same
# program on the fewest cores without cross-validation, and the RMSE and
# largest difference from the reference
agreement <- timings %>%
  mutate(
    own_run = paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv"),
    loglik_diff = loglik - loglik[run == reference_run],
    diff_own = mapply(
      function(run, own_run) max_diff(q_aligned[[run]], q_aligned[[own_run]]),
      run, own_run
    ),
    rmse_ref = vapply(run, function(r) rmse(q_aligned[[r]], q_ref), 0),
    diff_ref = vapply(run, function(r) max_diff(q_aligned[[r]], q_ref), 0)
  )
```

```{r numbers, include = FALSE}
# numbers for the text: the time of a run, the agreement of a program with
# ADMIXTURE (on the fewest cores, without cross-validation), and the largest
# difference between the runs of a program
time_of <- function(tool, n_cores, crossval = FALSE) {
  timings$seconds[
    timings$tool == tool & timings$n_cores == n_cores &
      timings$crossval == crossval
  ]
}
format_seconds <- function(x) {
  formatC(signif(x, 3), format = "fg", digits = 3, big.mark = ",")
}
format_diff <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x == 0, "0", formatC(signif(x, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2))
}
agreement_of <- function(tool, column) {
  agreement[[column]][agreement$run == paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv")]
}
runs_differ_by <- function(tool) {
  diff <- max(agreement$diff_own[agreement$tool == tool])
  if (diff == 0) {
    "identical ancestry proportions"
  } else {
    paste("ancestry proportions that differ by up to", format_diff(diff))
  }
}
```

## Summary

The three programs estimated the ancestry proportions of `r n_indiv`
individuals of the HGDP, typed at `r format(n_loci, big.mark = ",")` loci,
for K = `r k` ancestral populations (see [The data](#the-data)):

- On `r min_cores` core, without cross-validation, `gt_radmix()` took
  `r format_seconds(time_of("radmix", min_cores))` s, ADMIXTURE
  `r format_seconds(time_of("admixture", min_cores))` s and fastmixture
  `r format_seconds(time_of("fastmixture", min_cores))` s; on
  `r max_cores` cores, they took
  `r format_seconds(time_of("radmix", max_cores))` s,
  `r format_seconds(time_of("admixture", max_cores))` s and
  `r format_seconds(time_of("fastmixture", max_cores))` s.
- Compared with ADMIXTURE (on `r min_cores` core, without
  cross-validation), the log-likelihood of `gt_radmix()` differs by
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("radmix", "loglik_diff"))`, and that of
  fastmixture by `r format_diff(agreement_of("fastmixture", "loglik_diff"))`.
  Their ancestry proportions differ from those of ADMIXTURE by up to
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("radmix", "diff_ref"))` and
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("fastmixture", "diff_ref"))` respectively.
- Across numbers of cores, with and without cross-validation,
  `gt_radmix()` gives `r runs_differ_by("radmix")`, ADMIXTURE
  `r runs_differ_by("admixture")`, and fastmixture
  `r runs_differ_by("fastmixture")`.

## Do the programs find the same ancestry proportions?

All three programs maximise the same likelihood, but each starts from its
own random values and stops according to its own convergence criterion.
Each run is compared with ADMIXTURE on `r min_cores` core without
cross-validation, after matching its clusters to those of ADMIXTURE:

```{r table_agreement, echo = FALSE}
agreement %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores, crossval) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    crossval = if_else(crossval, "yes", "no"),
    loglik = formatC(loglik, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ","),
    across(c(loglik_diff, diff_own, rmse_ref, diff_ref), format_diff)
  ) %>%
  select(
    tool, n_cores, crossval, loglik, loglik_diff, diff_own, rmse_ref, diff_ref
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program", "Cores", "CV", "Log-likelihood", "Difference",
      "Largest difference (same program)", "RMSE (ADMIXTURE)",
      "Largest difference (ADMIXTURE)"
    ),
    align = "lllrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Log-likelihood of each run (fastmixture reports it with one decimal), ",
      "and its difference from that of ADMIXTURE on ", min_cores, " core ",
      "without cross-validation (CV; positive when higher). ",
      "Largest absolute difference between the ancestry proportions of each ",
      "run and those of the same program on ", min_cores, " core without ",
      "CV, and root mean square error (RMSE) and largest absolute difference ",
      "from those of ADMIXTURE on ", min_cores, " core without CV. The Q ",
      "matrices are stored with 6 decimals, so differences smaller than ",
      "1e-6 do not show."
    )
  )
```

The ancestry proportions from each program (on `r min_cores` core, without
cross-validation), with the individuals grouped by region and population:

```{r plot_q, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
# the regions of the HGDP, from west to east
region_levels <- c(
  "Africa", "Middle_East", "Europe", "Central_South_Asia", "East_Asia",
  "Oceania", "America"
)
# the individuals are ordered by region and population, and, within each
# population, by the ancestry (in the reference) from its main cluster
main_cluster <- vapply(
  split(seq_len(nrow(q_ref)), individuals$population),
  function(rows) which.max(colMeans(q_ref[rows, , drop = FALSE])),
  integer(1)
)
main_ancestry <- q_ref[cbind(
  seq_len(nrow(q_ref)),
  main_cluster[individuals$population]
)]
indiv_order <- order(
  factor(individuals$region, region_levels),
  individuals$population,
  -main_ancestry
)
q_long <- bind_rows(lapply(names(tool_labels), function(tool) {
  q <- q_aligned[[paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv")]][indiv_order, ]
  data.frame(
    tool = tool,
    individual = rep(seq_len(nrow(q)), k),
    region = rep(individuals$region[indiv_order], k),
    cluster = factor(rep(seq_len(k), each = nrow(q))),
    proportion = as.vector(q)
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = factor(tool, names(tool_labels)),
    region = factor(region, region_levels)
  )
# one colour per cluster (from the Okabe-Ito palette)
cluster_colours <- c(
  "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00",
  "#CC79A7", "#999999"
)
ggplot(q_long, aes(x = individual, y = proportion, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  facet_grid(
    tool ~ region,
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free_x",
    labeller = labeller(
      tool = tool_labels,
      region = function(x) gsub("_", " ", x)
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.spacing.x = unit(0.1, "lines"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0)
  )
```

## How long do they take?

```{r plot_timings, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# one colour per program
tool_colours <- c(
  radmix = "#2a78d6",
  admixture = "#eb6834",
  fastmixture = "#1baf7a"
)
timings %>%
  mutate(
    crossval = if_else(
      crossval,
      "With cross-validation",
      "Without cross-validation"
    ),
    crossval = factor(
      crossval,
      c("Without cross-validation", "With cross-validation")
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n_cores, y = seconds, colour = tool)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~crossval) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(timings$n_cores))) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = tool_colours, labels = tool_labels) +
  labs(x = "Cores", y = "Time (s, log scale)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
```

```{r table_timings, echo = FALSE}
timings %>%
  group_by(tool, crossval) %>%
  mutate(speed_up = seconds[n_cores == min_cores] / seconds) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(tool, n_cores, crossval, seconds, speed_up) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = crossval, values_from = c(seconds, speed_up)) %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    across(starts_with("seconds"), format_seconds),
    across(starts_with("speed_up"), ~ formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 1))
  ) %>%
  select(
    tool, n_cores, seconds_FALSE, speed_up_FALSE, seconds_TRUE, speed_up_TRUE
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program", "Cores", "Time (s)", "Speed-up", "Time with CV (s)",
      "Speed-up with CV"
    ),
    align = "lrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Time (s) taken by each run, without and with cross-validation (CV), ",
      "and speed-up relative to the run of the same program on ", min_cores,
      " core."
    )
  )
```

All the times include reading the data and saving the results.
ADMIXTURE and fastmixture read the bed file and write their estimates of Q
and P to text files. For `gt_radmix()`, the time includes reading
the bed file into a `gen_tibble` (and its backing file), and saving the
resulting `gt_admix` object, with Q and P, to an RDS file. In an analysis
with several values of K, or several runs, the `gen_tibble` would only be
read once.

## Cross-validation errors

```{r table_cv, echo = FALSE}
timings %>%
  filter(crossval) %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    cv_error = formatC(cv_error, format = "f", digits = 5)
  ) %>%
  select(tool, n_cores, cv_error) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_cores, values_from = cv_error) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program",
      paste(
        sort(unique(timings$n_cores)),
        if_else(sort(unique(timings$n_cores)) == 1, "core", "cores")
      )
    ),
    align = "lrrr",
    caption = "Cross-validation error of each program, on each number of cores."
  )
```

ADMIXTURE and `gt_radmix()` compute the same cross-validation error
(Alexander and Lange 2011): they hold out a fold of the genotypes, refit the
model on the others, and average the deviance of the held-out genotypes.
They draw the folds differently, so their errors are close but not
identical. fastmixture averages the same deviance, but holds out a fold of
the individuals rather than of the genotypes. The allele frequencies come
from the other individuals, but the ancestry of the held-out individuals is
estimated from their own genotypes, the same genotypes on which the error is
then computed. Its errors can be compared between values of K, but not with
those of the other two programs.

# How the benchmark was run

The benchmark is run with three scripts, in `vignettes/articles/code` (in
the source code of the package). The first prepares the data. The second
runs ADMIXTURE and fastmixture from the command line. The third runs
`gt_radmix()` in R. The results are read here from
`vignettes/articles/data/admixture_benchmark`. Each run is done once, as the
full runs take long enough for the variation between repeated runs to be
small. The code shown below is taken from these scripts. Timings depend on
the machine (see [Machine and software](#machine-and-software)), but the
differences between the programs should be similar on other machines.

## The data

The data are those of the HGDP used in the benchmark of `tidypopgen`
(1043 individuals typed at about 650,000 loci), downloaded from Zenodo:

```{r download, eval = FALSE}
```

and prepared as recommended in the manual of ADMIXTURE. The steps are the
same as in the analyses of the HGDP with `tidygenclust`:

```{r filter, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r ld-clumping, eval = FALSE}
```

All three programs are run on this bed file. A small subset of it is also
saved, to check the scripts quickly (see
[Running the benchmark again](#running-the-benchmark-again)):

```{r quick-data, eval = FALSE}
```

## Running ADMIXTURE and fastmixture

ADMIXTURE and fastmixture are run from the command line, with the same
settings as `gt_radmix()`:

```{bash cli-settings, eval = FALSE}
```

Each program is run on 1, 4 and 8 cores (with `-j` in ADMIXTURE and
`--threads` in fastmixture), with and without cross-validation (with
`--cv`), with these functions:

```{bash cli-functions, eval = FALSE}
```

and the time, Q matrix, log-likelihood, cross-validation error and number of
iterations of each run are saved:

```{bash cli-runs, eval = FALSE}
```

## Running gt_radmix()

`gt_radmix()` runs on a `gen_tibble`. Its parallel loops use OpenMP,
with `n_cores` threads. It only calls BLAS for small systems of K
equations, so BLAS is kept to a single thread:

```{r r-packages, eval = FALSE}
```

It is run with the same settings as ADMIXTURE and fastmixture:

```{r r-settings, eval = FALSE}
```

Each run reads the same bed file into a `gen_tibble`, runs
`gt_radmix()`, and saves the result to an RDS file:

```{r r-runs, eval = FALSE}
```

Each program stops when its own default convergence criterion is met.
ADMIXTURE stops when the log-likelihood increases by less than 1e-4 between
iterations. fastmixture checks every 5 iterations, and stops when the
log-likelihood, divided by the number of observed genotypes, has increased
by less than 1e-9. `gt_radmix()` stops when the relative change in
the log-likelihood is less than 1e-7. The numbers of iterations are not
comparable either. An iteration of fastmixture is a pass of accelerated EM
updates, first over mini-batches of the loci. An iteration of ADMIXTURE and
`gt_radmix()` updates all the parameters with block-wise Newton
steps.

## From the results to the tables and plots

The results are read, and the Q matrices aligned and compared, with this
code:

```{r, ref.label = c("results_packages", "read_results", "align_q", "agreement"), eval = FALSE}
```

## Running the benchmark again

To run the benchmark again (e.g. after changing `tidygenclust`, or on
another machine), install `tidygenclust` with `R CMD INSTALL`, rather than
loading it with `devtools::load_all()`, which compiles its C++ code without
optimisation. Also install ADMIXTURE and fastmixture, e.g. in the conda
environment created by `tgc_tools_install()`. Then run, from
`vignettes/articles`, on an otherwise idle machine with at least 8 cores:

```sh
cd vignettes/articles
Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_data.R
conda activate ctidygenclust
bash code/admixture_benchmark_cli.sh
Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_radmix.R
```

The first script downloads and prepares the data in `data/hgdp`, which is
not part of the repository, and only needs to be run once. The other two
overwrite the results in `data/admixture_benchmark`; then render this
article again. With the argument `quick`, the last two scripts run
everything on the small subset of the data, to check them in a few minutes.
They then save their results in `data/admixture_benchmark_quick`, which this
article can be rendered on with:

```r
rmarkdown::render(
  "admixture_benchmark.Rmd",
  params = list(results_dir = "data/admixture_benchmark_quick")
)
```

# References

estimation of ancestry in unrelated individuals. *Genome Research*, 19,
1655-1664.

Alexander, D. H. & Lange, K. (2011). Enhancements to the ADMIXTURE algorithm
for individual ancestry estimation. *BMC Bioinformatics*, 12, 246.

Ko, S., Chu, B. B., Peterson, D., Okenwa, C., Papp, J. C., Alexander, D. H.,
Sobel, E. M., Zhou, H. & Lange, K. L. (2023). Unsupervised discovery of
ancestry-informative markers and genetic admixture proportions in
biobank-scale datasets. *The American Journal of Human Genetics*, 110,
314-325.

Santander, C. G., Refoyo Martinez, A. & Meisner, J. (2024). Faster
model-based estimation of ancestry proportions. *Peer Community Journal*, 4,
e115.
